subject: Post-call: stakeholder map + decision criteria (latency / deployment / SLA)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: stakeholder map + decision criteria (latency / deployment / SLA)

Hey Alyssa — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can map the right team and prepare a short decision packet for Martin. Notes below are from our call (please correct anything I missed).

Summary of stakeholders (as discussed)
- Economic / final sign: Martin Hayes (CTO) — will sign or approve budget and partner selection.
- Security / compliance reviewer: Elena Cruz (CISO) — will validate SOC 2, data residency, and any pen test evidence.
- Procurement / contracting: Jordan Vale — vendor onboarding and PO terms.
- Day-to-day tech lead: you (Alyssa) + one of your engineers for integration.

Decision criteria you emphasized
- Latency: P99 target ideally <= 150–200 ms for user-facing inference (low tolerance for spikes).
- Cost: target unit economics ~ <$120 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot (we heard this as a guideline).
- Deployment preference: Private VPC / dedicated capacity due to PHI + residency requirements, though you asked about hybrid fallback.
- SLA: intent for a commercial SLA (>= 99.95%) for production. Pilot can have lighter SLA.

Questions we left open (can you confirm?)
1) Expected steady-state QPS for pilot and production targets (you said ~10 QPS in the call — can you give a range?).
2) Average/median sequence length for your telemetry (rough tokens per request; you mentioned ~512 words — want tokens).
3) Data residency: confirm US-only or specific region(s).
4) Procurement timeline: is Q4 2026 the target for pilot contracts? Who will sign the pilot SOW vs. final contract?
5) Any vendor security forms (e.g., ISV questionnaires) Jordan prefers we complete up front?

Next steps I suggest
- We’ll prepare a concise 1–2 page decision packet for Martin: cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs private), latency tradeoffs, and recommended rollout path (pilot canary -> production).
- Neha will draft two pricing options (pilot + production reserved capacity).
- Schedule a short security deep-dive with Elena and our security engineers — request Wed next week 11:00–11:30 PT if that works.

Attachments we’ll send after this thread: SOC2 summary, pilot SOW draft, a simple network requirements sheet you can share with infra.

Appreciate any clarifications on the questions above — will incorporate into the packet.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks

From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@brightwavehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Martin Hayes <martin.hayes@brightwavehealth.com>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@brightwavehealth.com>, Jordan Vale <jordan.vale@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: stakeholder map + decision criteria (latency / deployment / SLA)

Thanks Dylan — helpful notes, and confirmed below:

1) Stakeholders: correct. Martin will have final say; procurement is Jordan (he handles vendor forms and POs). Elena will do the security review and expects SOC 2 + recent pen test results or attestation.
2) QPS: pilot expected ~8–12 QPS peak; steady-state target for production around 25–40 QPS depending on feature rollout.
3) Sequence length: average request ~350 tokens; some batch analytics calls go up to ~2k tokens.
4) Data residency: US-only for now (we host patient data in US regions).
5) Timeline: aiming to kick off pilot procurement in early Q4 2026, pilot run in Q4, production H1 2027 if pilot meets SLA/latency.
6) Procurement forms: Jordan typically requests an initial vendor security questionnaire and a signed MSA or PO. He can share the vendor onboarding doc; I’ll loop him in separately.

We’ve attached a short network requirements XLSX (internal) that lists firewall and IP allowlist notes — hope that helps.

On latency: Elena flagged that end-to-end P99 < 200 ms is a hard bar for the user-facing UI; they’d expect backend inference to be in the 120–150 ms P99 range so front-end can hit the 200 ms goal.

For the pilot, Martin is open to a dedicated pool with an option to move to private (customer-managed VPC) if compliance requires it. He wants cost transparency for the two paths.

Happy to join a security call next Wed; 11:00 PT works for me and I'll invite Jordan and Elena formally.

Best,
Alyssa
Sr. Product Manager, BrightWave Health
alyssa.morgan@brightwavehealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: stakeholder map + decision criteria (latency / deployment / SLA)

Sounds good — two quick asks from GTM side:
1) Can you draft a 1-pager for Martin that compares three options (hosted API, Dedicated reserved pool, Private VPC) with bullets: cost delta, expected P99 latency, operational burden, and friction points for procurement? I can add pricing bands once you send rough capacity/QPS numbers.
2) Procurement usually needs a sample MSA plus SOW and an internal vendor form. If Jordan prefers DocuSign vs PO we should call that out.

On SLA — propose we offer a pilot SLA of 99.9% for 30 days and a commercial SLA of 99.95% for production; call this out in the packet as negotiable but benchmarked.

I’ll prep two pricing scenarios (pilot small reserved pool and production annual commit). Also add a suggested rollout: 2-week technical validation -> 30-day pilot -> production canary -> 30-day ramp.

If you want, I can join the security call and handle pricing questions live.

1) Security call: Wed 11:00 PT confirmed. I’ve invited Redwood security + Neha to join. Agenda: SOC 2 artifacts, pen test attestation, and network/IP allowlist.
2) Decision packet: Neha and I will deliver a 1–2 page comparison for Martin by Fri EOD (pricing bands + recommended rollout and SLA options).
3) Pilot SOW: drafting a short pilot SOW (30 days, defined QPS cap, measurement plan) — attached draft. Please confirm who signs the pilot SOW (Jordan or Martin?).
4) Procurement: Jordan — can you share the vendor onboarding form or tell us if a PO is sufficient for pilot?

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf; pilot-sow-draft.docx (draft).
